claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you with that.

You mentioned Alex is 16 and lives with you. At age 16, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He left school recently and has signed up with the local careers service to help him figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. This is helpful information.

Since Alex is 16, has left education or training, and has registered with a careers service, there's a specific provision that may apply to your situation. According to the rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service.

To help me assess this fully, I need to ask:

**When did Alex leave education, and approximately when did he register with the careers service?** (I need to understand if this happened recently or if it's been more than 20 weeks ago)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school just a few weeks ago, maybe around 6 or 7 weeks ago, and he registered with the careers service pretty much right after that - within a week or so of leaving.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?** (I'm asking because the 20-week extension applies to existing Child Benefit that can continue after a child leaves education)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him - this would be a new claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility.

Let me carefully consider your situation:

- Alex is 16 years old and lives with you in the UK
- He left school 6-7 weeks ago
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- He registered with the careers service shortly after leaving school
- This would be a new claim for Child Benefit

According to the Child Benefit rules, the 20-week extension that applies when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a careers service is specifically for **continuing** existing Child Benefit payments - it allows current payments to continue for up to 20 weeks in these circumstances.

However, since you are not currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex and this would be a new claim, this extension provision does not apply to your situation. For a new claim, Alex would need to be either:
- Under 16, OR
- Under 20 and staying in approved education or training

Since Alex is 16, not in approved education or training, and you're making a new claim (rather than continuing an existing one), you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him at this time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**However**, if Alex decides to return to approved education or training in the future while he's still under 20, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that point. The careers service he's registered with may help him find suitable training or educational opportunities.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
